summary.intent: Get started on the Lio 'Keep the Line Running' hackathon challenge for Soony: analyze the confidential supply-chain data drops, then build a general recheck-and-act agent product (poller, extraction, reconciliation, supplier emails with approval) and prepare for office-hours interviews.
summary.outcome: Found that Soony's launch plan hides real Collector's Edition shortfalls (overbooked art books, failed statues, stale tracker, pins without POs) and built a versioned poller, reconciled shipment tracking, floor site-question flow, editable approved emails and an outbox duplicate guard (288 tests passing), with several supplier emails sent. Briefing page and interview doc were also created.

repo: Portal API has only /files, /files/{path} and /archive.zip, no webhooks; the only way to detect drops is polling the file list and comparing SHA-256, since files are replaced under the same name.
Confidential portal data lives in the gitignored data/ folder; .env holds the token and .env.example is committed with an empty value.
The team's CLAUDE.md and PROGRESS.md define a workflow where tasks are claimed in PROGRESS.md before coding.

Hand-kept Excel tracker (soony/logistics/open_shipments_tracker_v37_FINAL_final2.xlsx) was previously read only by the verifier, while the app used only soony/erp/open_shipments.csv, which has been frozen since Fri 17:00.
Shipment status is reconciled by precedence: goods receipt, site answer, supplier document or reply, newer hand-kept tracker, system export, other sheets; documents never move a shipment backwards.

The server only sends emails to known supplier addresses (profile contact plus past reply senders), protecting against typos and forged-notice fraud; subject, To and CC are editable only within that set.

The mailbox is shared, so the app only sees what it sends itself; hand-sent mails and Lucas's Pulse console (origin/new-approach, pulse-console/server.mjs) bypass the allow-list and caused stray or duplicate emails.
Several JSON supplier profiles (Pune 'watch/conditional', PackRight 'at risk') contradict CSV 'active' status but only the email addresses were being read from them.
Local Entire hooks skip checkpointing when no repo files are modified during a turn.
workflow: Use a subagent for bulk cross-checking (200 order confirmations, 59 scans) and write findings to gitignored notes rather than code.
Check Entire logs (not just status) to verify hooks fired; checkpoints only appear on commits with changes.
Before committing, check whether parallel builder agents touched shared files so half-finished work isn't committed.
Verify each change with the full pytest suite, ruff and tsc before committing and restarting the server.
Hand-written emails should use full contact names from supplier profiles, never guessed titles or surnames from addresses.

friction: Portal token was initially empty, which blocked data access until the user supplied it.
Three hand-written supplier emails guessed salutations from addresses and got 'Mr Nowak' and 'Mr Rohan' wrong.
The shared mailbox let Lucas's Pulse console send unvetted emails (including one with order data to an external Gmail address) and let a manual order at 07:04 duplicate an in-app order sent at 06:50.
UI bugs: claim sentence wording and a stray period caused by block-level buttons, and the chosen option lacking a number and click target.
Rule for sign-off routing was evaluated before final case status was known, so art-book cards ended up in the wrong place.
The artifact page was published without a rendered preview check.
Portal data drops arrive without notice, and some formats (JSON profiles, DOCX memo, launch_status.xlsx, news) were read but not actually used by the app.
